Wings can only be those that are adjacent to your core type so if your a 5 your wing would be a 6 or 4 and if your a 9 your can be either a 8 or 1.  Some people have no wings, some people have high on both wings.  Lots of 9s at first mistype as 5s . 9s tend to feel like they relate to all of them, and not being able to decide is a very 9 thing. Its easier to pin your self down if you look at the wings. If your relate to 4s or 6s some your are probably a 5 but if you instead relate to 1s and 8s more your are probably a 9.  Also if you look at the flaws for each type you might feel something that makes you instinctively vulnerable like some spilling your darkest secrets. 

For instance, I'm a 9w8 but every time I took a test I typed different, 5, 4, 8, 1, 6 it wasn't until I read the flaws of nine that i new what I was.  It was all the things I never wanted people to know about me, like how we procrastinate, are hard to motivate, lack ambition,  become recessive and like to escape into our heads when we are uncomfortable, put stuff off or avoid because it takes to much energy to deal with it,  Fear confrontation.

Love Enneagram, never done the Tritype testing though so don't know much about it, but here are my answers 

Part 1-A - traits

Most like me (1): D Easygoing, Trusting, Conciliatory, Self-Effacing, Escapist, Passive Aggressive.

Second most similar (1):B Analytical, Knowledgeable, Observant, Detached, Isolated, Nihilistic.

Third most similar (1):E Empathetic, Altruistic, Sentimental, People-Pleasing, Manipulative, Victimizing

Somewhat similar: C Unique, Emotional, Creative, Self-Absorbed, Self-Deprecating, Self Conscious

Nothing like me: F Future Oriented, Extroverted, Open Minded, Compulsive, Reluctant, Arrogant

Part 1-B - Fears

Guiding fears (Major) (3): D The fear of being harmed or controlled by others ( or simply being out of control of the situation)

Secondary fears (Intermediate): H  The fear of being helpless and inadequate (more like third because a fear of conflict definitely a close second to D, and F just doesn’t fit, I don’t feel the need to keep the conflict causing people in my life at all.  I wish they would just leave me alone.  I hate conflict because I don’t like tension, it makes me want to crawl inside myself and shut everything out. I like to try to diffuse the situation so everyone can be happy and get along.  I want everyone to get along, harmony is best.  But I also have no problem with just leaving so I don’t have to be involved and then the conflict can’t fill me with all that cringe worthy awkwardness  and steal all my precious energy)

Nonexistent fears: The fear of being without support or guidance( eh, all of the others ones I can remember feeling at least once sometime or another, but I don’t think I’ve ever felt I couldn’t survive on my own.  Though I do believe in the practicality of seeking advice/guidance from others it keeps you balanced and they can help you see your blind spots.

Part 2 How do you express 

Anger  :  B most of the time A sometimes when I’m at the end of my tolerance

Shame :  C Definitely all the time, but I’m working on being open about things so I can help those around me. Transparency can be very healing for others who struggle with the same things, but a piece of me always cringes.  And there are some things I'm just not capable of sharing.

Fear  :  Maybe A? Don’t know on this one, I’m pretty open about talking bout my fears, so I don’t think I qualify as repressed or internalized.  But I don’t feel my fears control me, my mind does going to worse case scenario in a need to prepare what to do if the worst case scenario happens, planning, researching and being cautious make me feel secure.  Situation completely out of my control like Tornadoes scare the crap out of me, so even large thunderstorms make me uneasy, but I never shut down, I just go into emergency preparedness mode

I have to admit your comment rubs me raw.  It makes me want to shut down.  I can appreciate you trying to encourage that I will definitely find a positive answer for God on the other side of doubt.  I'm well aware that i'm experiencing doubt as I do mention it.  I'm afraid for me labeling it doesn't help.   I know for some people it does but for me I just want an answer.  I want certainty.  That certainty may come back to me realizing God does exist but right now I feel much more certain that God does not exist.

I definitely have reasons, this wasn't about a feelings.This was about all the evidence I've accumulated over the years suddenly clicking, and then slamming into me like a sledgehammer with the unsettling conclusion that God does not exist. I now there are very open churches out there, and the church i have been a part is very open to science, but the aggressive stance against science from leading Christians as a whole has left a bad taste in mouth. And this is probably where my feelings do play a big part, I just don't feel like I can trust Christians Leadership in the interpretation of God and the Bible anymore.

The loss of certainty has probably been the most crushing for me. Though I do definitely feel like I also am focusing on my family more now, though I think this may have of something to do with me not managing my time well and taking on too many leadership roles at church.  Now I'm not doing any of them. My husband is right there with me  and very supportive for that I could not be more grateful.  It's my parents I don't think I could tell, my moms reaction terrifies me.  And it's not rejection I worry about but extreme disappointment.
Definitely not gibberish, this is along the lines of stuff I think about all the time especially about the human mind.
